hints: Look carefully at the left diagram, a leaf in transverse section. The large central bundle in the midrib has two different tissues, one above and one below. Which one is xylem?
Remember which plant transport tissue needs hollow, lignified tubes with no cytoplasm to work. Those cells must die at maturity to leave an open lumen.
walkthrough:
**Identify the organs and bundles**

First, recognise what you are looking at. The left diagram is a leaf lamina with midrib, the middle is a stem with a ring of bundles, the right is a root with a central stele.

In each vascular bundle, xylem and phloem sit together but in a predictable position.

**Recall which plant cells are dead**

Most plant cells are living, even with a vacuole and wall. The big exception is xylem vessels and tracheids.

They are lignified, hollow, with no protoplast, no nucleus and no cytoplasm, so water can flow freely through them as a dead tube.

**Spot the xylem label**

In the leaf midrib, label A points to the upper part of the large bundle. That is the xylem, facing the upper epidermis. Label B points to phloem, and labels C and D point to living stem and root tissues like phloem, cortex or pericycle.

Therefore only region A contains dead cells.

options.A: Correct. A is the xylem in the leaf midrib vascular bundle. Xylem vessels and tracheids are dead, lignified and hollow for water transport.
options.B: B is phloem tissue in the leaf veins. Sieve tube elements and companion cells are living cells, so this is false.
options.C: C is living tissue in the stem bundle, the phloem region. Phloem cells are living at maturity, so this is false.
options.D: D is living tissue in the root stele, such as phloem or surrounding parenchyma. These cells retain cytoplasm and nuclei, so this is false.
